[Who I work with]{.eyebrow}

## One foundation, three ways to work together
:::

::: {.aud}
::: {.aud-item}
### Recruiters and research teams

A biostatistician who supports researchers from question to paper.

- Choosing and critiquing methods
- Methods sections, publication-ready figures
- FAIR data, version-controlled code
:::
::: {.aud-item}
### Public bodies and consultancies

A technical partner for tenders and territorial diagnostics.

- Open data (INSEE, BAN, OSM)
- Mapping at census-tract and municipal level
- Demonstrators delivered quickly
:::
::: {.aud-item}
### Colleagues and students

Training and tools to become self-sufficient.

- Workshops on R, Git, reproducible pipelines
- Documented packages and apps
- Explaining results in plain terms
:::
:::
:::

[An unusual path]{.eyebrow}

## Physicist by training, statistician by practice

I don't hold a statistics degree. I hold a PhD in physics, where measurement, uncertainty and modelling are daily work, followed by fifteen years of practice reviewed by peers: journals, a hackathon jury, hospital research teams.

::: {.btns}
[Read my story](about.qmd){.btn}
:::
:::

1. PhD in physics (highest honours): measurement, uncertainty and inverse modelling
2. Continuous training in statistics since 2012 (Stanford, Duke, Johns Hopkins…)
3. 4 years and 9 months as senior biostatistician at Montpellier University Hospital
4. Methods vetted by peer review in health and climate journals
:::
:::
